title: Route Method and Path Together
concept: Separate unknown routes from disallowed methods

writing.summary: Separate unknown routes from disallowed methods.
writing.rule: Resolve the resource first, then the allowed HTTP method.
writing.explanation:
An HTTP method is part of the request contract. GET /tasks lists tasks; POST /tasks creates one. A known resource with a disallowed method is different from a path the application does not own. This lab returns 405 for unsupported methods on /tasks and 404 for unknown paths; GET /health returns 200, while other health methods return 405.

The request target can include a query string. Separate it before matching the path, but do not lowercase the path or decode arbitrary escapes without a policy: route names can be case sensitive. The lab implements literal paths only. A desktop Axum router handles the transport; the on-device adapter passes a bounded real HTTP request to Rust through stdin. It is an HTTP/1.x adapter with one response per connection, not an implementation of every HTTP version or chunked body mode.

The route project is Task Ledger: first keep a reproducible source history, then expose its data through a CLI and HTTP boundary, persist it in SQL, diagnose failures and prepare a release. This lesson owns one contract in that project. Run the worked example before changing the starter and explain which input makes the tempting shortcut fail.

Terminal practice: Run cargo serve --port 8080 --database tasks.db, then curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/tasks and curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8080/tasks. Stop with http stop.

The compiler lab is independent of the reading question. Edit solution.rs; the app supplies a separate caller with normal, empty and adversarial inputs. A successful unchanged demonstration does not prove your implementation. After the lab, apply the same contract to the route companion project. Its README separates the on-device adapter from the desktop Cargo/TCP profile.
writing.exampleCaption: The worked implementation exercises separate unknown routes from disallowed methods. Its tests demonstrate the stated finite contract.
writing.task: Match literal /tasks and /health after removing the query string. GET tasks=200, POST tasks=201, GET health=200; other methods on those paths=405, unknown paths=404. Keep the public signature. Open the compiler lab and edit solution.rs; do not edit the private verification caller.
writing.success: The separate caller accepts the changed solution and rejects unchanged TODO, a wrong implementation and a printed success message.
writing.question: What distinguishes 405 from 404 in this routing contract?
answers: Both statuses always mean the same thing
An unknown path should return 200 with an empty body
The resource exists but the method is disallowed
writing.feedback: Matching only a method or only a path loses the distinction between unsupported operations and unknown resources.

depth.misconception: Both statuses always mean the same thing
depth.correction: Resolve the resource first, then the allowed HTTP method.
